title: H_1 of the naive cotangent complex of a field over F_p vanishes
statement: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, an $\mathbf F_p$-algebra in the unique way. Then $H_1(L_{K/\mathbf F_p})=0$, where $H_1(L_{K/\mathbf F_p})$ is the first homology of the naive cotangent complex of the canonical presentation $\mathbf F_p[K]\to K$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 0322 (proposition-characterize-separable-field-extensions, line 44475), characteristic p, (1) => (5), applied with k = F_p, which is perfect (Definition Tag 030Y, line 10489: every extension of a perfect field is separable; Lemma Tag 030Z, line 10495: F_p is perfect as x^p = x on F_p); used in More on Algebra, proof of Proposition 07E5 ('H_1(L_{K/F_p}) = 0 as K/F_p is separable'); tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: *Every finitely generated extension of $\mathbf F_p$ is separable.* Let $E/\mathbf F_p$ be a finitely generated field extension, $E=\mathbf F_p(a_1,\dots,a_n)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-make-separable] there are a field $E''$ with a field homomorphism $\iota:E\to E''$ and a subfield $k'\subseteq E''$ containing the image $P$ of $\mathbf F_p$ (the prime field of $E''$) such that $k'/P$ and $E''/\iota(E)$ are finite purely inseparable and $E''$ is separable over $k'$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (2). First, $k'=P$: let $\alpha\in k'$; by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] $c:=\alpha^{p^m}\in P$ for some $m\ge0$; every element of $P\cong\mathbf F_p$ satisfies $c^p=c$ (Fermat), so $c^{p^m}=c$ and $(\alpha-c)^{p^m}=\alpha^{p^m}-c^{p^m}=c-c=0$ ($x\mapsto x^p$ is additive in characteristic $p$); $E''$ is a field, so $\alpha=c\in P$. Hence $E''$ is separable over $P$. Now let $E'\subseteq E$ be a subextension finitely generated over $\mathbf F_p$, $E'=\mathbf F_p(b_1,\dots,b_r)$. The field homomorphism $\iota$ is injective and is the identity on prime fields, so $\iota(E')=P(\iota(b_1),\dots,\iota(b_r))$ is a finitely generated subextension of $E''/P$ and is therefore separably generated over $P$ (definition (2) for $E''/P$): it has a transcendence basis $(y_j)$ over $P$ with $\iota(E')/P(y_j)$ separable algebraic. Transporting along the isomorphism of fields $\iota|_{E'}:E'\to\iota(E')$, which is the identity on prime fields, $(\iota^{-1}(y_j))$ is a transcendence basis of $E'/\mathbf F_p$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] and $E'/\mathbf F_p(\iota^{-1}(y_j))$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] (an isomorphism preserves algebraic independence, algebraicity and minimal polynomials). So every finitely generated subextension of $E/\mathbf F_p$ is separably generated, i.e. $E$ is separable over $\mathbf F_p$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (2). (This replaces the source's appeal to Definition 030Y / Lemma 030Z, '$\mathbf F_p$ is perfect, so every extension is separable', by 030R for $k=\mathbf F_p$, where the purely inseparable $k'$ is forced to be $\mathbf F_p$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 030R (lemma-make-separable, line 10513) with k = F_p, in place of Definition Tag 030Y (definition-perfect, line 10489) and Lemma Tag 030Z (lemma-perfect, line 10495); Definition Tag 030O (definition-separable-field-extension, line 9915)

proof.text: *$H_1$ vanishes for finitely generated subextensions.* Let $E\subseteq K$ be a subfield finitely generated over $\mathbf F_p$. By step 1, $E/\mathbf F_p$ is separable, so by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-fraction-field-of-smooth-algebra] there is an $\mathbf F_p$-subalgebra $B\subseteq E$ with $\mathbf F_p\to B$ smooth and $E$ the fraction field of $B$. By condition (ii) of smoothness [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], $H_1(L_{B/\mathbf F_p})=0$. $B$ is a domain, so $T=B\setminus\{0\}$ is multiplicative; by [lem-weil-pbc-h1-cotangent-localization] (with $R=\mathbf F_p$, $A=B$) $H_1(L_{T^{-1}B/\mathbf F_p})\cong T^{-1}H_1(L_{B/\mathbf F_p})=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The $\mathbf F_p$-algebra map $\sigma:T^{-1}B\to E$, $b/t\mapsto bt^{-1}$, is well defined ($t\ne0$ is a unit of $E$), surjective (every element of $E$ is $b/b'$ with $b'\neq0$) and injective ($bt^{-1}=0$ forces $b=0$), hence an isomorphism. The $\mathbf F_p$-algebra isomorphism $\Sigma:\mathbf F_p[T^{-1}B]\to\mathbf F_p[E]$, $[x]\mapsto[\sigma(x)]$ (renaming the variables [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]), satisfies $\gamma_E\circ\Sigma=\sigma\circ\gamma_{T^{-1}B}$ for the canonical presentations, so it maps $I_{T^{-1}B}=\ker\gamma_{T^{-1}B}$ onto $I_E=\ker\gamma_E$ and $I_{T^{-1}B}^2$ onto $I_E^2$; and $\partial\Sigma(g)/\partial[\sigma(x)]=\Sigma(\partial g/\partial[x])$, so $g\bmod I^2\mapsto\Sigma(g)\bmod I_E^2$ is a bijection $I_{T^{-1}B}/I_{T^{-1}B}^2\to I_E/I_E^2$ carrying the kernel of $\delta$ onto the kernel of $\delta_E$ (the differentials of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]). Hence $H_1(L_{E/\mathbf F_p})\cong H_1(L_{T^{-1}B/\mathbf F_p})=0$.

proof.text: *Reduction to finitely generated subextensions.* Let $\gamma:\mathbf F_p[K]\to K$ be the canonical presentation, $I=\ker\gamma$, so that $H_1(L_{K/\mathbf F_p})=\ker(\delta:I/I^2\to\bigoplus_{s\in K}K\,\mathrm d[s])$ with $\delta(g\bmod I^2)=\sum_s\gamma(\partial g/\partial[s])\,\mathrm d[s]$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Let $\xi=g\bmod I^2\in H_1(L_{K/\mathbf F_p})$, $g\in I$; thus $\gamma(\partial g/\partial[s])=0$ for every $s\in K$. The polynomial $g$ involves only finitely many variables $[s_1],\dots,[s_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; let $E=\mathbf F_p(s_1,\dots,s_m)\subseteq K$. The polynomial ring $\mathbf F_p[E]$ on the variables $[s]$, $s\in E$, is the subring of $\mathbf F_p[K]$ of polynomials in these variables, it contains $g$ and is stable under $\partial/\partial[s]$ for $s\in E$, and its canonical presentation $\gamma_E$ is the restriction of $\gamma$ (both send $[s]$ to $s$). Hence $\gamma_E(g)=\gamma(g)=0$, i.e. $g\in I_E=\ker\gamma_E$, and $\gamma_E(\partial g/\partial[s])=\gamma(\partial g/\partial[s])=0$ in $E\subseteq K$ for every $s\in E$; so $g\bmod I_E^2$ lies in $H_1(L_{E/\mathbf F_p})$, which is $0$ by step 2. Thus $g\in I_E^2$, i.e. $g=\sum_if_ih_i$ with $f_i,h_i\in I_E\subseteq I$, so $g\in I^2$ and $\xi=0$. Therefore $H_1(L_{K/\mathbf F_p})=0$.
